meta: Part 1 of "AI and your job". Instead of asking "will AI take my job?", this video sees a job as a bundle of small tasks. Using a teacher as an example, it shows AI takes tasks, not whole jobs.

muc.title: What will happen to your job?
muc.text: AI can do so much now. What will happen to your job? This five-part series gives honest answers, no scare tactics. Part one: AI replaces tasks, not jobs.

muc.title: A job is a bundle of tasks
muc.text: A job isn't just one task. It's a bundle of many small tasks. A teacher writes tests, grades work, teaches, talks with parents and encourages students.

muc.title: AI pulls out one stick at a time
muc.text: AI pulls out the small tasks it can do, like drafting a test or grading multiple choice. But it can't pull out the whole bundle.

muc.title: People who use AI get ahead
muc.text: So the biggest risk usually isn't AI. It's someone in your field who knows how to use AI and works faster than you.

muc.title: Time freed up
muc.text: The work AI helps with gives you back time. Spend that time on the parts only people can do.

muc.title: List 10 tasks from your week
muc.text: List ten things you do each week. Mark the ones AI could help with, even partly. That's where to start.

muc.title: Which tasks does AI take first?
muc.text: But which tasks is AI taking over fastest? Part two has three signs so you can spot them yourself.
